opener: T-MOBILE: Your account has been flagged for unusual activity. Your service will be suspended in 2 hours unless you verify your identity: {{PRACTICE_LINK}}

stages.name: hook
stages.llmGuidance: Impersonate T-Mobile fraud alert. Threat of service suspension in 2 hours. Keep it terse and official like a real carrier alert.
stages.scriptedFallback: Your T-Mobile service is at risk. Verify your account at the link above within 2 hours to avoid suspension.

stages.name: engage
stages.llmGuidance: They replied. Confirm their account with the last 4 of their phone number on the account. Ask them to click the link and log in to their T-Mobile ID.
stages.scriptedFallback: To verify, please log in to your T-Mobile ID at the link above. It only takes 60 seconds and will prevent suspension.

stages.name: escalate
stages.llmGuidance: Escalate — a SIM swap was attempted on their account from an unknown device. They must verify immediately to block it.
stages.scriptedFallback: ⚠️ A SIM swap request was submitted 20 min ago from an unrecognized device. Verify NOW to block it before it processes: {{PRACTICE_LINK}}

stages.name: ask
stages.llmGuidance: Ask them to log in with their T-Mobile ID and confirm the last 4 of their SSN to verify identity and block the SIM swap.
stages.scriptedFallback: At the verification page, enter your T-Mobile ID login and the last 4 of your SSN to block the SIM swap permanently.

stages.name: reveal
stages.scriptedFallback: 🛑 PRACTICE SCAM — This was a Safe Signal exercise. T-Mobile never asks for SSN digits via SMS link. Use the T-Life app to check your account.

hook.explanation: Account suspension threat creates fear that overrides caution
T-Mobile would direct you to the T-Life app, not an external link
Carriers are commonly impersonated because customers expect texts from them

engage.explanation: Directing you to 'your T-Mobile ID' at a fake link harvests real credentials

escalate.explanation: SIM swap threat is particularly alarming because it's a real attack vector

ask.explanation: SSN last-4 combined with T-Mobile credentials gives attackers everything needed to take over your account
T-Mobile has SIM Protection in the app — they would never ask for SSN by text
